# BINDING CONSISTENCY LEDGER — Northern Welsh (Colloquial Gogledd Cymru Welsh) Listening Pod

## 1. TRANSLITERATION
TRANSLITERATION: not needed — names stay as written.

## 2. PRICES
- £3 → tair punt
- £5.50 → pump punt a hanner
- £6–£8 (coffee + cake) → rhyw saith punt
- £4.50–£6 (pint) → rhyw bum punt
- £8.40 (Scene 7 total) → wyth punt dau ddeg
- £12.50 (Scene 14 taxi) → deuddeg punt hanner

## 3. TARGET-LANGUAGE NAME
**Cymraeg** — used identically in all scenes where the language is named aloud.

## 4. RECURRING LINES

| Canonical | Northern Welsh (Colloquial) |
|-----------|---------------------------|
| Good morning. | Bore da. |
| Good afternoon. | Prynhawn da. |
| Good evening. | Noswaith dda. |
| What can I get you? | Be alla i 'i gael i chdi? |
| Thank you very much. Goodbye. | Diolch yn fawr. Hwyl. |
| Excuse me. | Scusio fi. |
| Pleased to meet you. | Tŷ lân 'i chi gwrdd â chdi. |
| Where are you from? | O ble dach chi'n dwad? |
| I'm learning Northern Welsh. | Dw i'n dysgu Cymraeg. |
| Could you say that again more slowly? | Fedri di ddeud hynna eto'n arafach? |
| I'd like a [drink], please. | Liciwn i [drink], os gweli di'n dda. |
| Would you like to sit-in or takeaway? | Yma isio di'r gwmnniaeth neu mynd â fo? |
| Could I pay by card? Do you have contactless? | Fedra i dalu â cherdyn? Oes gynnoch chi dap? |
| Are you here on holiday? | Wyt ti yma ar wyliau? |
| You speak very good Northern Welsh. | Dach chi'n siarad Cymraeg yn dda iawn. |
| Thank you very much, and goodbye. | Diolch yn fawr, a hwyl. |
| Excuse me, do you know how to get to [place]? | Scusio fi, wyt ti'n gwybod sut i fynd i [place]? |
| Thank you very much. You've been very helpful. | Diolch yn fawr. Ti 'di bod yn dda iawn. |
| Can you take me to [place], please? | Fedri di fy nymryd i i [place], os gweli di'n dda? |
| Could I pay by card? | Fedra i dalu â cherdyn? |
| I'm learning Northern Welsh. I need to practise more to speak Northern Welsh better. | Dw i'n dysgu Cymraeg. Dw i angen ymarfer mwy i siarad Cymraeg yn well. |
| You seem to speak it very well. I can understand you easily. | Dach chi'n siarad yn dda iawn. Dw i'n dallt chi'n iawn. |
| I don't understand people very well when they don't speak slowly. | Dw i ddim yn dallt pobol yn dda iawn pan dydyn nhw ddim yn siarad yn araf. |

## 5. REGISTER

**Unmarked polite register throughout:** Use **ti** universally for all service workers (barista, bartender, shop assistant, pharmacist, taxi driver, hotel receptionist), strangers, acquaintances, and peers. Politeness is carried through softening particles ("os gweli di'n dda", "diolch yn fawr") rather than pronoun formality. No character uses "chi" except where the scene explicitly marks formal institutional context (none in this pod). 

**Softening particles:** Questions often drop auxiliary verbs and use rising tone; polite requests use "os gweli di'n dda" (if you please) naturally one or twice per scene, not excessively. One or two "diolch" per speaker per scene is natural; do not cluster multiple thanks.

sentences.speaker: Customer
sentences.target_text: Dw i wedi cael cur pen… a gwddw drwg ers ddoe.
sentences.known_text: I've had a headache and a sore throat since yesterday.

sentences.speaker: Pharmacist
sentences.target_text: Triwch barasetamol… at y cur pen,…a'r losenni yma… at y gwddw.
sentences.known_text: Try paracetamol for the headache, and these lozenges for the throat.

sentences.speaker: Customer
sentences.target_text: Pa mor aml ddylwn i gymryd… y parasetamol?
sentences.known_text: How often should I take the paracetamol?

sentences.speaker: Pharmacist
sentences.target_text: Un bob pedair i chwe awr,… dim mwy nag wyth mewn diwrnod.
sentences.known_text: One every four to six hours, no more than eight in a day.

sentences.speaker: Customer
sentences.target_text: Ydi hi'n iawn… i'w cymryd efo bwyd?
sentences.known_text: Is it all right to take them with food?

sentences.speaker: Pharmacist
sentences.target_text: Ydi, efo bwyd… neu ar ôl bwyd sydd orau.
sentences.known_text: Yes, with food or after food is best.

sentences.speaker: Customer
sentences.target_text: Diolch yn fawr. Fedra i gael… paced o blasters hefyd?
sentences.known_text: Thank you very much. Could I also get a packet of plasters?

sentences.speaker: Narrator
sentences.target_text: Un deg naw. Dau ddeg. Dau ddeg un. Dydd Mercher. Dydd Iau.
sentences.known_text: Nineteen. Twenty. Twenty-one. Wednesday. Thursday.

sentences.speaker: Tourist
sentences.target_text: Esgusodwch fi,… dach chi'n gwybod sut i fynd… i'r archfarchnad agosa?
sentences.known_text: Excuse me, do you know how to get to the nearest supermarket?

sentences.speaker: Local
sentences.target_text: Ydw,… mae hi tua deng munud… o gerddad. Ewch yn syth… ar hyd y ffordd yma.
sentences.known_text: Yes, it's about a ten minute walk. Go straight along this road.

sentences.speaker: Tourist
sentences.target_text: Heibio'r eglwys yna?
sentences.known_text: Past that church?

sentences.speaker: Local
sentences.target_text: Ia,… heibio'r eglwys a'r… swyddfa bost.
sentences.known_text: Yes, past the church and the post office.

sentences.speaker: Local
sentences.target_text: Wrth yr ail gylchfan,… cymrwch yr allanfa gynta.
sentences.known_text: At the second roundabout, take the first exit.

sentences.speaker: Tourist
sentences.target_text: A wedyn?
sentences.known_text: And then?

sentences.speaker: Local
sentences.target_text: Mi welwch chi'r archfarchnad… ar eich chwith,… yn union gyferbyn… â'r safle bws.
sentences.known_text: You'll see the supermarket on your left, just opposite the bus stop.

sentences.speaker: Tourist
sentences.target_text: Ardderchog. Ac oes 'na beiriant arian… yn agos?
sentences.known_text: Wonderful. And is there a cashpoint nearby?

sentences.speaker: Local
sentences.target_text: Oes, mae 'na un ar y stryd fawr,… wrth ymyl y becws.
sentences.known_text: Yes, there's one on the high street, next to the bakery.

sentences.speaker: Tourist
sentences.target_text: Diolch yn fawr. Dach chi wedi bod yn help mawr.
sentences.known_text: Thank you very much. You've been very helpful.

sentences.speaker: Narrator
sentences.target_text: Tri deg. Pedwar deg. Pum deg. Dydd Gwener. Dydd Sadwrn.
sentences.known_text: Thirty. Forty. Fifty. Friday. Saturday.

sentences.speaker: Passenger
sentences.target_text: Helo. Fedrwch chi fynd â fi… i'r orsaf drenau… os gwelwch yn dda?
sentences.known_text: Hello. Can you take me to the train station, please?

sentences.speaker: Driver
sentences.target_text: Medra, wrth gwrs. Falla bydd o'n cymryd… dipyn o amser,… mae 'na lot o draffig… ar hyn o bryd.
sentences.known_text: Yes, of course. Perhaps it will take some time, there's a lot of traffic at the moment.

sentences.speaker: Passenger
sentences.target_text: Tua faint o amser… dach chi'n meddwl… bydd o'n ei gymryd?
sentences.known_text: About how long do you think it will take?

sentences.speaker: Driver
sentences.target_text: Falla tua ugain munud,… os nad ydan… ni'n anlwcus… efo'r goleuadau traffig.
sentences.known_text: Perhaps about twenty minutes, if we're not unlucky with the traffic lights.

sentences.speaker: Passenger
sentences.target_text: Dach chi'n gwybod… ble fedra i gael tocyn… yn yr orsaf?
sentences.known_text: Do you know where I can get a ticket in the station?

sentences.speaker: Driver
sentences.target_text: Yndw, mi adawa i chi… reit wrth y swyddfa docynnau.
sentences.known_text: Yes, I'll leave you right by the ticket office.

sentences.speaker: Driver
sentences.target_text: Dyma ni. Deuddeg punt pum deg… ydi hynna.
sentences.known_text: Here we are. That's twelve pound fifty.

sentences.speaker: Passenger
sentences.target_text: Fedra i dalu… efo cerdyn?
sentences.known_text: Could I pay by card?

sentences.speaker: Driver
sentences.target_text: Medrwch, wrth gwrs. Mae'r peiriant reit fan hyn.
sentences.known_text: Yes, of course. The machine is right here.

sentences.speaker: Narrator
sentences.target_text: Cant. Dau gant. Mil. Dydd Sul. Deuddeg o'r gloch.
sentences.known_text: One hundred. Two hundred. One thousand. Sunday. Twelve o'clock.

sentences.speaker: Learner
sentences.target_text: Faset ti'n meindio… taswn i'n trio ymarfer… siarad Cymraeg efo chdi? Dw i ddim wedi bod… yn dysgu ers amser hir iawn… a dw i'n dal i deimlo… chydig bach yn nerfus… wrth siarad… efo pobol eraill.
sentences.known_text: Would you mind if I tried to practise speaking Welsh with you? I haven't been learning for very long, and I still feel a little nervous about speaking with other people.

sentences.speaker: Friend
sentences.target_text: Wrth gwrs, dim problem. Ti i'w weld… yn siarad yn dda iawn. Dw i'n dallt chdi'n iawn.
sentences.known_text: Of course, no problem. You seem to speak it very well. I can understand you easily.

sentences.speaker: Learner
sentences.target_text: Diolch, mae'n dda gwybod hynna. Dw i angen dysgu… mwy o eiriau,… ac mae angen i mi… ymarfer gwrando. Dw i ddim yn dallt pobol… yn dda iawn… pan dydyn nhw ddim yn siarad… yn araf.
sentences.known_text: Thank you, that's good to know. I need to learn more words, and I need to practise listening. I don't understand people very well when they don't speak slowly.

sentences.speaker: Friend
sentences.target_text: Ydw i'n siarad… yn ddigon araf… i chdi rŵan?
sentences.known_text: Am I speaking slowly enough for you now?

sentences.speaker: Learner
sentences.target_text: Wyt, diolch. Mae'n haws siarad… efo un person yn unig. Mae o chydig bach yn anodd… meddwl am rywbeth i'w ddeud,… cofia. Dw i ddim yn… siŵr be i'w ddeud,… ond dw i'n teimlo… fel taswn i'n… gallu siarad… digon i ddechrau cael sgyrsiau.
sentences.known_text: Yes, thank you. It's easier talking to just one person. It's a bit difficult thinking of something to say, though. I'm not sure what to say, but I feel as if I can speak enough to start having conversations.

sentences.speaker: Friend
sentences.target_text: Dw i'n meddwl… dy fod ti'n gwneud… yn dda iawn. Dw i wedi synnu. Dw i'n meddwl… dy fod ti'n barod… i ddechrau siarad Cymraeg… efo unrhyw un… sy'n siarad Cymraeg.
sentences.known_text: I think you're doing very well. I'm impressed. I think you're ready to start speaking Welsh to anyone who speaks Welsh.

sentences.speaker: Learner
sentences.target_text: Mae o chydig bach… yn rhwystredig… pan dw i ddim yn gallu… meddwl yn ddigon cyflym… i fynegi fy hun yn iawn. Ond dw i'n gwybod… bod angen i mi ddal ati… i ymarfer… os dw i isio siarad… yn fwy hyderus.
sentences.known_text: It's just a little frustrating when I can't think quickly enough to express myself properly. But I know that I need to keep practising if I want to speak more confidently.

sentences.speaker: Friend
sentences.target_text: Dylat ti fod yn hyderus… yn barod. Dw i'n meddwl… dy fod ti'n gwneud… yn llawer gwell… na ti'n sylweddoli. Dw i'n… teimlo'n gyfforddus… yn siarad efo chdi,… a dw i ddim yn siarad… yn araf iawn.
sentences.known_text: You should be confident already. I think you're doing much better than you realise. I feel comfortable speaking with you, and I'm not talking very slowly.

sentences.speaker: Learner
sentences.target_text: Dyma'r union… fath o ymarfer… sydd ei angen arna i. Dw i'n meddwl… y galla i deimlo… fo'n newid fy ymennydd i… tra dan ni'n siarad! Dw i wir yn gwerthfawrogi… dy help di. Ond mae'n syndod… pa mor flinedig… dw i'n mynd… pan dw i'n siarad mewn iaith… dw i ddim yn ei siarad… yn dda iawn.
sentences.known_text: This is exactly the kind of practice I need. I think I can feel it changing my brain while we're talking! I really appreciate your help. But it's surprising how tired I get when I'm talking in a language I don't speak very well.

sentences.speaker: Friend
sentences.target_text: Dw i'n meddwl… bod hynna'n normal. Mae dysgu iaith newydd… yn anodd. Ond mae o'n gymaint o hwyl… pan ti'n dechrau cael sgwrs… tydy?
sentences.known_text: I think that's normal. Learning a new language is difficult. But it's so much fun when you start to have conversations, isn't it?

sentences.speaker: Learner
sentences.target_text: Ydy, wir. Dw i wir yn hapus… y galla i gael… cymaint o sgwrs â hyn. A dw i'n gobeithio… y byddwn ni'n gallu cael… mwy o sgyrsiau… yn y dyfodol… wrth i mi ddal ati… i wella.
sentences.known_text: It really is. I'm really happy that I can have this much of a conversation. And I hope we'll be able to have more conversations in the future as I keep on getting better.

sentences.speaker: Narrator
sentences.target_text: Can mil. Chwe deg. Saith deg. Un o'r gloch. Un ar ddeg o'r gloch.
sentences.known_text: A hundred thousand. Sixty. Seventy. One o'clock. Eleven o'clock.
